newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo tea auction prices rise on lower volumes.
newsitem.headline: Colombo tea auction prices rise on lower volumes.

text.p: Sri Lankan tea prices rose virtually across the board at Colombo's auction because of lower quantities and impoved demand, brokers said on Wednesday.

"Prices of most of categories of tea improved," said a broker at Forbes and Walker. "There is a shortfall in the crop here and around the world. Prices at most other auction centres are above ours and importers are looking to Colombo for their requirements."
The anticipated gross auction average price for the 4.8 million kg on offer rose to 102.50 rupees ($1.77) per kg from 102.19 rupees last week, Forbes and Walker said.
Better Western BOPs were two to four rupees dearer and best Uva/ Udapussellawa BOPs rose by similiar amounts.
The Commonwealth of Independent States, the biggest buyer of Ceylon tea, was active but selective for poor teas, brokers said.
There was more interest from South Africa, the United Kingdom, Pakistan, Japan and Egypt.
The next auction is on April 1-2 where 5.0 million kg will be on offer. ($1=57.78 rupees) --Colombo newsroom (941) 434319
